data.title: AS-75 F7/F8: document the manual bootstrap and the COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME scrub that makes a test deploy hit production

data.to:
From the AS-75 QA review (qa-ruben), findings F7 and F8. Both are documentation, and F8 has already cost a day of downtime.

F8 (the expensive one). performDeploy hands docker a deliberately scrubbed environment which DROPS COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME. That is correct for production — it makes the deploy immune to whatever env a tick happens to carry — but it means -p and COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME cannot isolate a test deploy: the compose file's own 'name: asc-chat' always wins. During this very review, Ruben set COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME to isolate a harness run of the real makeDeployOps; the scrub discarded it and the deploy recreated the LIVE asc-chat-server-1 from his scratch copy — a copy with the ports mapping and the ../..:/repo:ro mount stripped. 127.0.0.1:8347 was unreachable until the orchestrator rebuilt from master. The trap is invisible in the code at the call site and there is no note anywhere.

F7. Neither README says that the feature cannot deploy itself: the first deploy after AS-75 merges must be bootstrapped by hand (rebuild + watcher restart), because the running container and the running watcher both predate the code that would have deployed them. A reader who merges and waits will conclude the mechanism is broken.

ACCEPTANCE. Both facts documented where someone testing or merging this will actually hit them (apps/chat/watch/README.md and apps/chat/README.md). For F8, prefer a guard over prose if one is cheap: a test deploy that targets a non-production project should fail loudly rather than silently retarget production. Exact proposed wording for both is recorded in Ruben's review comment on AS-75.

data.body: PLANNED (cto-owen, tick watcher:92536 loop tick 4). Key decisions. F7 is NOT moot — the AS-75 bootstrap happened (merge a0cfb0b 2026-09-07, first unattended deploy 31a934e same day, first unattended self-restart 5d7c5f8 2026-09-11) so Ruben's instruction is past tense, but the rule behind it recurs (a deploy mechanism cannot deploy the first version of itself; the self-restart digest covers watch/*.mjs only, so the plist and its ADVANCE_* knobs, compose.yaml's name:/port map, and a hand-run watcher still need a hand) — rewritten as one sentence of dated history + the rule + the current hand list, plus a rewrite of watch/README.md § 'After any change to this watcher: restart it', whose first sentence has been false since AS-75. F8 is guard AND prose. Measured on the real compose.yaml (Compose v5.3.0, 'docker compose config'): -p beats COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME beats name: — Ruben's 'name: always wins' is wrong as a compose fact and right as a watcher fact only because runDockerCompose passes no -p and performDeploy's seven-key env drops the variable; the README states the cause. Guard (~15 lines, zero production behaviour change): PRODUCTION_COMPOSE_PROJECT='asc-chat' pinned to compose.yaml; runDockerCompose always passes -p <composeProject> and throws without one; makeDeployOps REQUIRES composeProject (no default; makeWatcher passes the production constant) and REFUSES at construction when a non-empty COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME in its env differs from composeProject (Ruben's exact input is AC-4's observed red). No pass-through of the variable — AS-87 §8's default is withdrawn (amended in its plan this tick), and the existing seven-key env pin at watcher.test.js:934 is named as that falsifier (AC-6). 13 ACs, 10 mutants, +8 host tests (all docker-free, compose moves +8, skipped set unchanged), predicted post-AS-87 529 -> 537 relative to a measured baseline. Seam: assumes AS-84 and AS-87 on master; overlap sites are the runDockerCompose argv line, makeDeployOps options, performDeploy's deploy({}) object, makeWatcher's wiring comment, the § AS-75 README section (disjoint hunks), AS-87's argv pin (AS-88 edits it: +'-p') and AS-87's opt-in real-build test (gains composeProject — without it that test would run -p asc-chat on a foreign compose file inside the live project, which is the guard doing its job on our own test). Reviewer probe to run down: does a thrown makeDeployOps inside makeWatcher.start() actually crash-loop under launchd as the README paragraph claims, or is it swallowed — if swallowed, the sentence changes. Implementer developer-lena (free; wrote the scrub in AS-75), reviewer qa-priya (Ruben authored the base wording — anchoring), complexity low-medium, branch feat/AS-88-deploy-names-its-project from post-AS-87 master. Default if the board declines the production change: land §4 prose alone and file the guard with §3/§5 as its plan.

Implementation complete on feat/AS-88-deploy-names-its-project, head e5a180a (two commits, both developer-lena: 9a61bad code+tests, e5a180a READMEs). Not moved to review — orchestrator does that.

FINDINGS / DECISIONS (before the sweep):
1. Plan §10 Q2 answered, twice. By reading: makeWatcher.start() wraps nothing around makeDeployOps() and main() calls watcher.start() bare, so a refusal is an uncaught exception -> exit 1 -> launchd relaunch. Empirically: mutant M8 (drop the wiring line) turned the three watcher-process.test.js entry-point tests red because the REAL process died at start(). The README crash-loop sentence is therefore true as written; I tightened it to say WHY (nothing catches it) and pointed it at the existing 'known failure mode' paragraph. Nothing filed.
2. The guard found two makeDeployOps/runDockerCompose callers plan §7 did not list: AS-84's stream-error test (direct runDockerCompose call, watcher.test.js) and AS-86's git-backed harness (deploy-inputs-git.test.js). Both now pass composeProject 'asc-test'. This is the 'forgotten path' being closed on our own suite — recorded so the reviewer knows two more tests another task owns were touched (plus AS-87's argv pin, which the plan named).
3. makeWatcher's env/exists (AS-92) do NOT reach makeDeployOps — it reads process.env/existsSync itself, so the plan's 'env with an unresolvable docker' for AC-8 has no wiring to go through. Left as is (out of scope, production behaviour unchanged; the refusal reading process.env is exactly what the launchd case needs). AC-8's test is still safe: start() fires no deploy evaluate synchronously. Noted in the test comment.
4. AC-12 optional real build RUN and passed: AS87_REAL_BUILD=1 ADVANCE_DOCKER_BIN=/usr/local/bin/docker, 92.8 s, 1/1, with composeProject = the scratch basename passed as -p; AC-11 footprint clean; compose ls afterwards shows no scratch project (asc-chat, asc-invoicing, bettereads, whatever-sticks only).
5. Deviation from plan wording, small: in the bootstrap paragraph's hand list I added 'change PRODUCTION_COMPOSE_PROJECT with it or test/deploy-shape.test.js fails' to the compose.yaml name: item — a renamed project now has two places to change, and the README should say so. No claim dropped anywhere; the launchctl print command in §4.1b is given in full rather than elided.
6. Compose skipped count is 7, not the 6 AS-87 and AS-92 each reported: each branch's own skip (AS-87 opt-in, AS-92 real-process) was 'the sixth' alone and both survive the merge. AS-88 adds zero skips; all 8 new tests ran in-container.

AC SWEEP (floor check, after the findings above): AC-1..AC-9 each met by an observed red (table below). AC-10 prose: §4.1a/b/c and §4.2a/b landed per plan; the reviewer re-derives each claim independently per the plan (I did not pre-run the docker compose config matrix — that is hers to do cold). AC-11: commits AS-88: <imperative> as developer-lena; zero .lattice paths; no top-level markdown; package.json unchanged (8 files, all under apps/chat). AC-12: watcher-process.test.js host tests pass with -p in argv; real build run (finding 4). AC-13: below.

HOST: baseline (pre-change, worktree at 28a54fd) 542 tests / 541 pass / 1 skipped / 0 fail -> final 550 / 549 / 1 skipped / 0 fail (+8, as predicted: 7 AS-88-titled + 1 deploy-shape).
COMPOSE: docker compose -p asc-impl-as88 run --build --rm test (absolute /usr/local/bin/docker via spawnSync): 'Image asc-impl-as88-test Built'; 550 tests / 543 pass / 7 skipped / 0 fail, exit 0. Torn down with down --rmi local --remove-orphans; no asc-impl-as88 container, network or image remains; asc-chat-server-1 Up (healthy) throughout.

MUTANTS (10 named, each on a fresh git archive of e5a180a, anchor asserted unique 1->0 at the site, red set net of an unmutated control whose only red is deploy-shape's git-dependent guard — no .git in an archive): 10/10 red, 0 survivors.
M1 (AC-1 drop -p) -> {AS-87 argv pin, AS-88 names the caller's project} exact. M1b (AC-1 literal asc-chat) -> {AS-88 names the caller's project} exact. M2 (AC-2 drop guard) -> {AS-88 refuses an implicit project} exact. M3 (AC-3 hard-code in performDeploy) -> {AS-88 performDeploy passes through} exact. M4 (AC-4 drop envIntent block) -> {AS-88 refuses COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME} exact. M5 (AC-5 drop equality) -> {AS-88 accepts agreeing/empty} exact. M6 (AC-6 pass-through) -> {AS-75 key-set pin} exact. M7 (AC-7 default) -> {AS-88 requires composeProject} exact. M8 (AC-8 drop wiring) -> {AS-88 makeWatcher production project, + AS-82 entry point heartbeat, AS-84 entry point SIGTERM mid-build, AS-84 entry point SIGKILL at grace} — WIDER than predicted (1 -> 4): prediction error, see finding 1. M9 (AC-9 asc-chat2) -> {deploy-shape name pin, AS-88 makeWatcher} exact.
Tree proven clean after (git diff --exit-code); merge-tree --write-tree master..branch clean. Battery script + logs in scratchpad/agent-developer-lena/ (as88-mutants.mjs, as88-mutants.log, as88-compose-receipt.txt, as88-real-build.txt).

Left undone: nothing in scope. Out of scope, for a separate note if anyone wants it: the Env knobs line in watch/README.md predates AS-92 and does not list ADVANCE_GH_BIN / ADVANCE_TICK_PATH_EXTRA (AS-92's paragraph does).

REVIEW (qa-priya, cycle 1, head 60a2d6e = Lena's e5a180a + one inline comment fix). VERDICT: PASS. Zero blocking findings; 1 inline fix; 2 notes. Findings first, sweep second (M5).

FINDINGS (outside the criteria list, M6):
F1 (fixed inline, comment-only, 60a2d6e): the AC-5 test comment claimed compose treats a whitespace COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME as unset, 'measured, plan §0.1'. §0.1 measured only the empty string. Re-measured with docker compose config (v5.3.0, absolute path, env limited to PATH/HOME): COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME='  ' -> exit 1 'invalid project name "  "'. Not a behaviour defect — the scrub drops the variable before compose sees it, so treating whitespace as 'no intent' in the guard is correct — but the comment stated a measurement that was never taken. Rewritten to say what was measured; no code changed.
F2 (note, not a criterion): a composeProject that is non-empty but invalid to compose (leading '-', a space, uppercase) passes both guards, opens the deploy log, spawns compose, and fails with compose's own 'invalid project name' in deploy-*.log and outcome 'fail'. Plan §5's probe candidate expected no log to be opened; I judge the actual behaviour acceptable — the reason is in the log and nothing touches a stack — and note it for a backlog item (mirror compose's name regex in the guard) only if someone wants it.
F3 (note): master's own scratch-copy baseline shows 'deploy-shape: every tracked path under apps/chat…' red on a git-archive copy sitting in an untracked dir (git ls-files walks up to the main repo). Environmental, identical on master and branch archives, subtracted from every mutant tally below; green in the worktree.
Q2 (plan §10) answered from source: makeWatcher.start() (:2732) wraps nothing around makeDeployOps; main() (:2874) calls watcher.start() bare. The refusal is an uncaught throw -> exit 1 -> launchd relaunch -> crash-loop with the reason on stderr (launchd.err.log). README sentence is TRUE. Confirmed empirically by M8: the three real-process entry-point tests (AS-82/AS-84) die when the wiring line is removed.

RECEIPTS (cardinality before pass rate):
- Host, worktree apps/chat, explicit cwd: 550 tests / 549 pass / 1 skipped (AS87_REAL_BUILD opt-in) / 0 fail. Master archive: 542 (-> +8 as the plan predicted).
- Compose, -p asc-review-as88, --build: 'Image asc-review-as88-test Built'; 550 / 543 pass / 7 skipped / 0 fail, exit 0 (7 skipped = AS-84 git-dependent real-process tests + AS-87 opt-in, unchanged from post-AS-87). Torn down with down --remove-orphans; asc-review-as88_default network removed, none left; asc-chat-server-1 untouched (Up, healthy) before and after. Every compose call I issued carried -p asc-review-as88.
- Merge-tree master..feat/AS-88 at 60a2d6e: clean (c5db34e1).

MUTANTS: 10 named, 10 run on per-mutant copies of a git-archive scratch tree (worktree never mutated), each anchored to a site-unique string with the count transition asserted (1->0, or 0->1 for the M6 insertion), F3's env red subtracted. 10 red, 0 survivors.
M1 (drop -p) -> AS-87 argv pin + AS-88 'names the caller's project' [2, as predicted]. M1b (literal 'asc-chat') -> 'names the caller's project' only [1, as predicted — M1/M1b distinguishable]. M2 (drop runDockerCompose guard) -> 'refuses an implicit project' [1, predicted]. M3 (hard-code in performDeploy) -> 'passes composeProject through' [1, predicted]. M4 (drop envIntent block) -> 'refuses a COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME the scrub would discard' [1, predicted]. M5 (drop equality clause) -> 'accepts an agreeing or empty COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME' [1, predicted]. M6 (pass-through) -> existing AS-75 env key-set pin [1, predicted — the pre-existing falsifier does its job]. M7 (default to PRODUCTION_COMPOSE_PROJECT) -> 'requires composeProject' [1, predicted]. M8 (drop wiring line) -> 'makeWatcher deploys to the production project' + AS-82 entry point + 2x AS-84 entry point [4, plan predicted 1 — wider because the real process crashes on start; a prediction error, and the proof of Q2]. M9 ('asc-chat2') -> deploy-shape name pin + makeWatcher test [2, as predicted — both recorded].

FLOOR CHECK (labelled as such; AC-1..AC-13 sweep):
AC-1 pass (M1, M1b red; argv exact). AC-2 pass (M2 red; 5 implicit shapes, zero spawns/zero logs asserted). AC-3 pass (M3 red; log line 'DEPLOY building <id> (project asc-scratch-1) ->'). AC-4 pass (M4 red; Ruben's exact input; message names both values and 'pass composeProject'; symmetric case also covered). AC-5 pass (M5 red; 5 constructions). AC-6 pass (M6 red against the :1080 key-set pin, seven keys read: CHAT_BUILD_ID, COMPOSE_DOCKER_CLI_BUILD, DOCKER_BUILDKIT, HOME, LOGNAME, PATH, USER; no pass-through). AC-7 pass (M7 red; 4 shapes incl. null). AC-8 pass (M8 red; ops().deploy.composeProject === 'asc-chat' under real process.env). AC-9 pass (M9 red in two places). AC-10 pass — each claim re-derived: (i) seven keys from the pin; (ii) precedence matrix repeated with /usr/local/bin/docker compose config: asc-chat / foo / bar / bar / asc-chat, v5.3.0; (iii) AC-1; (iv) AC-4; (v) AS-75 merged a0cfb0b 2026-09-07, kickstart asked in dafec10 same day, first unattended deploy 31a934e 2026-09-07, self-restart 5d7c5f8 2026-09-11 on AS-82; (vi) readWatchSources filters .mjs only (:746); (vii) restartWatcher calls exit(70) with no launchd check (:1173). Cross-references 'known failure mode' (:268), 'Uninstall / restart' (:396), 'self-restart contract' (:214) all resolve. AC-11 pass (2 commits as developer-lena, AS-88: prefix; no .lattice/, top-level md, or package.json in the diff). AC-12 pass for the host half (watcher-process tests green at 550/549); the opt-in real build NOT run by me (time box) — Lena's 92.8 s run stands as the only record. AC-13 pass (receipts above).
Sweep: 13/13 with 3 findings outside the list (1 fixed, 2 notes). Nothing needs the board.
